brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A strip-shaped green tea, both basket-dried and pan-fired, grown mainly around Chongru township in Xiapu, Fujian. Funing was the Ming-era name of Xiapu, and the tea is picked before the Lantern Festival, Yuanxiao.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: It was developed in 1991 from the early-budding variety called Chunfen Cha. It reaches the market early and sells well in large cities. Little more is documented about it.
processing: Fixed, rolled, given a first drying, shaped by pan rolling, spread, fired again, then sorted and packed.
harvest_season: Before the Lantern Festival, tender green shoots.
appearance_dry: Fine, slender, curled strips of silvery green.
appearance_wet: Usually soft green leaf that opens up in the water.
taste_profile: High aroma and a mellow, full taste.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
